# Case 216: Overload Added Beside an `initializer_list` Overload

**Category:** Overloads | **Verdict:** ✅ COMPATIBLE

## Verdict and consumer impact

Negative control for
`case111`.
`mylib::pick(int)` and `mylib::pick(std::initializer_list<int>)` exist; v2
adds `mylib::pick(double)`. `pick(int)` and `pick(double)` both accept `{}`
by the identity conversion, so judged as a pair they look ambiguous. But
the `initializer_list` overload ranks better for a braced argument
([over.ics.rank]/3.1), so `mylib::pick({})` selects it before and after:
GCC and Clang return 2 both ways. Before the 2026-10-11 re-audit fix,
abicheck reported `overload_ambiguity_introduced` here.

## Old/new diff

| v1.h | v2.h |
|---|---|
| `int pick(int);`<br>`int pick(std::initializer_list<int>);` | same, plus `int pick(double);` |

## abicheck command

```bash
g++ -shared -fPIC -g v1.cpp -o libv1.so
g++ -shared -fPIC -g v2.cpp -o libv2.so
abicheck compare libv1.so libv2.so --header old=v1.h --header new=v2.h
```

## Expected abicheck finding

```text
Verdict: COMPATIBLE (exit 0)
  func_added  mylib::pick(double)
  (no overload_ambiguity_introduced)
```

Same result with the CastXML and the Clang header backend
(`ABICHECK_AST_FRONTEND=castxml|clang`).

## Minimum evidence

`L0` (symbol table): the new `pick(double)` export alone shows the addition. The negative claim -- no `overload_ambiguity_introduced` -- is about the header tier, where the overload witness is computed.

## Why abicheck catches it

The ambiguity witness is checked against the whole overload set: another
overload taking `std::initializer_list` at the `{}` position wins the call,
so no ambiguity is claimed.

## Runtime failure demonstration

```bash
g++ app.cpp -L. -l:libv1.so -Wl,-rpath,. -o app && ./app       # pick({}) = 2
sed 's/v1.h/v2.h/' app.cpp > app2.cpp && g++ app2.cpp v2.cpp -o app2 && ./app2   # pick({}) = 2
```

## Safe redesign

Nothing to fix: this is a compatible addition.
